title: Equivariant product internal Hom preserves quasi-isomorphisms into K-injective targets
statement:
Let $(C,J,R)$ be a ringed site small in the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention], with $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Let $s$ be an automorphism of its sheaf topos with a specified ring isomorphism $s^{-1}R\simeq R$, and let $T=s^*$ be the induced additive exact autoequivalence of $\mathcal C=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $\mathcal W=\mathcal C^T$ for fixed pairs $(M,\theta_M:TM\xrightarrow{\sim}M)$ and intertwining morphisms [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], and $U:\mathcal W\to\mathcal C$ for forgetting the structure. Put $H(M,N)=\mathcal Hom_R(UM,UN)$, where internal sheaf Hom sends a localized site object $V$ to the $R|_V$-linear sheaf maps $UM|_V\to UN|_V$. Give it the conjugation structure $h\mapsto\theta_N T(h)\theta_M^{-1}$, using the pullback comparison for internal Hom. For integer-indexed complexes define
$$H^\bullet(K,I)^n=\prod_{p\in\mathbf Z}H(K^p,I^{p+n}),\qquad d(f)=d_I f-(-1)^n f d_K.$$
Products are taken in $\mathcal W$. A complex is K-injective if every chain map into it from an acyclic complex is null-homotopic. Use the ordinary derived categories and quasi-isomorphisms of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

The functor $U$ creates these products, is exact and detects quasi-isomorphisms, and sends K-injective complexes to K-injective complexes. There is a natural identification of complexes
$$UH^\bullet(K,I)\simeq\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(UK,UI)$$
with the product terms and differential displayed above. If $t:K'\to K$ is any quasi-isomorphism of complexes in $\mathcal W$ and $v:I'\to I$ is a quasi-isomorphism between K-injective complexes in $\mathcal W$, then
$$H^\bullet(t,v):H^\bullet(K,I')\longrightarrow H^\bullet(K',I),\qquad f\longmapsto v f t,$$
is an equivariant chain map and a quasi-isomorphism. Thus its image under $Q_{\mathcal W}$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal W)$. No boundedness, local freeness, tensor exactness, or exactness of infinite products is assumed.

proof.text: The category $\mathcal C=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], since the site is small in the specified universe. Its small limits can also be constructed directly: over each site object take the compatible tuples in the product of the diagram's sections, with coordinatewise scalars and restrictions. Compatible local tuples glue uniquely coordinatewise, so this is a sheaf and has the limit universal property. Small colimits exist by the cited Grothendieck assertion. Thus [lem-sf-fixed-pair-created-abelian-structure] applies to the given additive autoequivalence $T$: $\mathcal W$ is abelian and $U$ creates the integer-indexed products and is exact and conservative. In particular the underlying product of the $H(K^p,I^{p+n})$ is the ordinary product of the internal sheaf Homs.

proof.text:
Use the internal-Hom pullback comparison specified in the statement, and write $\Theta_{M,N}(f)=\theta_N T(f)\theta_M^{-1}$. The comparison $T\mathcal Hom_R(UM,UN)\to\mathcal Hom_R(TUM,TUN)$ is an isomorphism, natural in both variables, because $T=s^*$ is part of an equivalence of ringed topoi (quasi-inverse $(s^{-1})^*$, using the specified ring isomorphism), and an equivalence carries the internal Hom, defined by $R$-linear maps over every localized object, to the internal Hom. Composing it with conjugation by the isomorphisms $\theta_N$ and $\theta_M^{-1}$ gives an isomorphism $TH(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(M,N)$, so $(H(M,N),\Theta_{M,N})$ is a fixed pair, and postcomposition and precomposition with morphisms of $\mathcal W$ are morphisms of $\mathcal W$ by the two identities below. Naturality of that comparison and the intertwining identities give
$$\Theta_{K^p,I^{p+n+1}}(d_I f)=d_I\Theta_{K^p,I^{p+n}}(f),\qquad
\Theta_{K^{p-1},I^{p+n}}(f d_K)=\Theta_{K^p,I^{p+n}}(f)d_K.$$
Hence the signed differential is a morphism of fixed pairs. Expanding its square gives $d_I^2f-fd_K^2=0$, because the two mixed terms have opposite signs. Creation of products in step 1 therefore gives the asserted identification $UH^\bullet(K,I)\simeq\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(UK,UI)$: in degree $n$ it is the map whose projections are the identity on every internal-Hom factor. Both differentials have those same projections. This proves compatibility with differentials and naturality, without asserting exactness of products.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), the displayed product terms and signed differential; conjugation calculation for the fixed-pair structure.

proof.text:
Define $H^n(t,v)$ by its $p$-th component $f_p\mapsto v^{p+n}f_p t^p$. On such a component equivariance is the identity
$$\theta_I T(vft)\theta_{K'}^{-1}
=v\theta_{I'}T(f)\theta_K^{-1}t,$$
obtained by substituting $\theta_I T(v)=v\theta_{I'}$ and $T(t)\theta_{K'}^{-1}=\theta_K^{-1}t$. Moreover
$$d(vft)=v(d_I'f-(-1)^n f d_K)t$$
since $v$ and $t$ commute with the differentials. The universal property of the products makes these component identities the required equivariant chain-map identity. Under step 3 its underlying map is precisely the ordinary internal-Hom map $f\mapsto(Uv)f(Ut)$.

source.place: Tag 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined), its induced Hom-complex morphism, with the explicit conjugation check.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] to $Ut:UK'\to UK$ and $Uv:UI'\to UI$. Step 2 verifies its quasi-isomorphism and K-injectivity hypotheses, and steps 3-4 identify its actual Hom-complex morphism with $UH^\bullet(t,v)$. It follows that $UH^\bullet(t,v)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The kernel/cokernel and conservativity argument of step 2 then shows that $H^\bullet(t,v)$ is a quasi-isomorphism in $\mathcal W$. Finally $Q_{\mathcal W}$ inverts this map by the definition of the derived-category localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All these inputs apply to unbounded complexes and require no local freeness or tensor exactness.
